From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Sara Khan <sara.khan@mendotahealth.com>
Cc: gregory.li@techops.mendotahealth.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: CS boarding priorities, technical blockers, and owner assignments for Mendota Health

Hi team —

We closed Mendota this morning; deal ID DEAL-83471. High level: enterprise pilot for 6 months (US west region), expected ramp to 1000 monthly active inference calls by month 3. Sara is the product lead and Greg is their infra/tech ops contact. Key asks up front: VPC peering, SOC2 evidence, and token-level cost reporting in the Console.

Attachments: Mendota_SOW_v1.2.pdf (proposed SOW), network_architecture_diagram.png (their requested layout), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (timeline + milestones).

Immediate asks for CS:
- Primary CS lead: assign and introduce by EOD Tuesday (10/27).
- 60/90/120 day milestones in mutual_action_plan.xlsx need sign-off.
- Technical intake call with Greg (30–45 min) to confirm VPC setup and firewall rules; proposed window Tue/Wed morning PT.
- SOC2 evidence request: Sara will send a short questionnaire; we need RACI for who pulls the artifacts.

Internal notes / risks:
- Customer will require data residency for logs — want 90-day retention window; verify if we can map retention policies per tenant without custom infra.
- They asked for an aggressive cutover on 11/15; that leaves little runway for dedicated capacity if needed.

Marissa — could you own the kickoff and SOW review? Ben — can you be our point on the network/VPC items and run the intake? Tessa — please prep the acceptance criteria and escalation path docs.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CS boarding priorities, technical blockers, and owner assignments for Mendota Health

Thanks Jonas — excited to get started. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot scope: will run across two pilot clinics (IDs attached in the Drive link). We need weekly short syncs (30 mins) for the first 6 weeks.
2) VPC peering: we prefer a managed peering approach; Greg will map the IP ranges and restrictions on our end.
3) SOC2 artifacts: we’ll send the questionnaire today; ideally we get the artifacts within 5 business days.
4) Acceptance criteria: primary must-haves are latency under 350ms p50 for 512-token requests and consistent embedding accuracy per the sample evals we shared.

Proposed times for intake call with Greg: Tue 10/27 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 10/28 09:00–09:45 PT. Either works for us.

Sara Khan
Director, Product — Mendota Health
sara.khan@mendotahealth.com

2) SOW review: I’ll run a 30-minute SOW walkthrough with Sara + Greg tomorrow 10/27 at 11:00 PT (I’ll send calendar invite). Please review Mendota_SOW_v1.2.pdf prior to the call — I’ve highlighted the acceptance criteria section.
3) Weekly sync cadence: set to every Wed for first 6 weeks (30 mins) — Tessa, please create the recurring calendar and the shared notes doc.

Open items for Ben on tech: VPC peering timing, whether Dedicated capacity is required for 11/15 target, and the exact firewall ports needed. Ben — can you confirm by EOD today? If dedicated GPUs are needed we’ll need a quick decision window to reserve.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CS boarding priorities, technical blockers, and owner assignments for Mendota Health

Marissa / Jonas — quick technical notes: 

1) VPC peering: on our side we support two models — managed peering (preferred) or customer-managed peering. Managed peering will need the following ports opened outbound from Mendota: 443 (API), 2379 (etcd for internal metrics, only if they opt-in), and a range for KV cache replication if they request higher availability (will confirm).
2) Dedicated capacity: if Mendota wants the 11/15 cutover with the 1000 monthly active calls forecast, we will likely need to reserve a dedicated GPU pool for their traffic pattern. ETA to reserve is within 48 hours of decision.
3) Data retention: we can support tenant-level log retention policies down to a 30/90/365 day bucket model. If they require 90-day only with strict deletion guarantees, need Legal sign-off for the SLA language — cc’ing Legal in a follow-up.

Action items: I’ll run the intake with Greg today at 11:00 PT and circulate a short tech-readout doc (network diagram annotated + port list).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: network_architecture_diagram.png (annotated version to follow)
